review.notes: Built on the course: CS vs service, lifecycle, logo and revenue churn, CRR, GRR, CLV, TTV, handover, kickoff, SMART success criteria, leading vs lagging, health score build, thresholds, value vs health matrix, success plan. Calculations checked. Fictional company.

content.company: Ledgerline (fictional), selling inventory software to distributors on yearly contracts
content.briefing: You manage 40 business customers. Renewals are falling and the CEO wants to know why. You must onboard new customers well, spot risk early and protect revenue.

variants.text: You started the year with 200 customers and lost 8. What is logo churn?

choices.f: Customers lost / customers at start = 8 / 200.
8 is the count, not the rate.
That is the share kept.

variants.text: Starting recurring revenue Kz 100 m. Lost to churn Kz 6 m, downgrades Kz 4 m, upsell Kz 12 m. What is gross revenue retention?

choices.f: (100 - 6 - 4) / 100. GRR excludes expansion.
That includes upsell, which is net retention.
Downgrades also reduce GRR.

variants.text: Start: 200 customers. End: 210. New this year: 30. What is customer retention rate?

choices.f: That counts new customers as retained.

variants.text: A customer pays Kz 2 m a year at 60% gross margin and stays about 5 years. What is CLV?

choices.f: That ignores gross margin.
That is one year of margin.

variants.text: Contract signed 1 March. First value milestone, first stock count in the system, reached 15 April. What is time-to-value?

choices.f: Milestone date minus contract start. Shorter TTV lowers churn.
Close, but count the days: 45.
Dates make it easy to track.

variants.text: What must the sales-to-CS handover include?

choices.f: You do not overpromise or miss a hidden opponent.
The contract does not show what the customer expects.
Commercial terms are not the success story.

variants.text: At the kickoff meeting, what must be agreed?

choices.t: Roles, sponsor, success criteria and plan
choices.f: Clarity on who, what success means and when.
Features come in training, not kickoff.
Not the purpose of kickoff.

variants.text: Which is a SMART success criterion for a new customer?

choices.f: Metric, baseline, target and date.
Not measurable or timed.
Activity, not an outcome.

variants.text: Which is a leading indicator of churn risk?

choices.t: Falling weekly logins and lost sponsor
choices.f: Leading signals show risk while you can still act.
That is lagging; it already happened.
Lagging and too old.

variants.text: Health score: usage 80 (weight 40%), outcomes 60 (40%), relationship 50 (20%). Score and colour (green 75+, amber 50-74, red below 50)?

choices.f: That is the simple average. Apply weights.
That uses usage only.

variants.text: A large customer pays the most but its health is red. Where does it sit, and what do you do?

choices.f: Executive attention and a recovery plan now.
Upselling an unhappy customer accelerates churn.
Too little attention for the biggest risk.

variants.text: Last year's churned accounts all had green health scores before leaving. What do you do?

choices.f: The score missed the real signals. Adjust and review regularly.

choices.t: Trust the score; churn was bad luck
choices.f: A score that misses churn is not working.
Improve it rather than drop it.

variants.text: A customer turns amber. What should happen?

choices.t: A defined action for amber, with an owner
choices.f: Each colour triggers a play.

choices.t: Wait to see if it turns red
choices.f: Waiting loses the time to act.
Discounts rarely fix the cause.

variants.text: The customer's executive sponsor leaves the company.

choices.t: Treat it as a risk; find a new sponsor
choices.f: Relationship change is a key leading signal.

choices.t: No impact; users still log in
choices.f: Without a sponsor, renewals are at risk.
Too late to rebuild the relationship.

variants.text: How does customer success differ from customer service?

choices.f: CS drives outcomes before problems appear.
Service fixes issues; success drives value.
Growth follows value, not the other way.

variants.text: What is the goal of the success plan written in?

choices.f: Their goal, with metric, baseline, target and date.
Features are means, not their goal.
Those are your goals, not theirs.

variants.text: A green, high-value customer reached all goals. What next?

choices.t: Grow: new goals, expansion and advocacy
choices.f: Expand and advocate is the lifecycle's last stage.

choices.t: Leave them alone; they are fine
choices.f: Safe, but you miss growth and referrals.
They are healthy, not at risk.

variants.text: In what order does the lifecycle run?

choices.f: Value comes before renewal and expansion.
Renewal comes after value.
You cannot expand before adoption.

variants.text: Training for all users is planned as one 3-hour session. What is better?

choices.t: Short training by role, then practice
choices.f: Training and adoption by role builds real use.
More time in one go does not build habits.
Manuals rarely drive adoption.

variants.text: The onboarding plan has no first value milestone.

choices.f: An early win proves value and lowers churn.
Customers who see no early value disengage.
Signing is not value for the customer.
